rationale: almabench is a floating-point numeric benchmark dominated by one or a few large hot loops containing mostly double-precision arithmetic and few calls or global accesses, and with the function-level profile unavailable the weighting must be robust to that structure. SUB gets the highest diversity weighting and low cost/risk scores because integer/pointer arithmetic substitution is cheap, composes well with other passes, and FP ops are typically skipped, making it safe for the hot kernel; SPLIT is weighted as a low-cost enabler that increases block count and thereby improves the effectiveness of FLA and BCF. FLA receives the highest SecurityGain since flattening the loop/nesting structure is the strongest structural deterrent for a program whose control flow is otherwise simple, but its moderate RuntimeCost/CorrectnessRisk scores prevent over-application on the innermost FP loop where dispatch overhead and loop-carried transformation bugs would hurt most. BCF is kept at a solid but tempered weight (opaque predicates add real resistance but inflate both code size and branch pressure in hot loops), and IBR is middling — indirect branches add resistance on the few real control edges but cost indirect-branch predictor performance in tight loops. ICALL and IGV are included but scored low on security/diversity because almabench has an almost call-free, mostly stack-resident FP kernel with minimal global state, so indirect calls and global-variable indirection would add overhead and correctness surface with little to hide.
